subject: Ingress bridge patterns: security, latency, and observability for Private deployments
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@finassure.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@finassure.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment networking — quick ask on best ingress pattern

Hi Nikhil,

We're kicking off the technical evaluation for running Redwood Private inside our VPCs and want to confirm the recommended ingress patterns. Our security team is hypersensitive to cross-VPC exposure, and our platform team cares about tail latency for inference (95th percentile). Can you help us:

- Outline the tradeoffs between VPC Peering, PrivateLink (VPCE), and Site-to-Site VPN for our use case (FinAssure handles PII and has strict audit requirements).
- Call out any compliance or observability gaps for each approach.
- Suggest a short checklist we can run with our network team to validate feasibility.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min call if that's easier.

— Alice
Alice Turner
Principal Cloud Engineer, FinAssure
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@finassure.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking — quick ask on best ingress pattern

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear asks. High level summary up front: each pattern can work for Private deployments, but the right choice depends on priorities (latency, isolation, observability, operational overhead). I attached a short option matrix and an observability checklist.

Quick tradeoffs (TL;DR):
- VPC Peering: lowest-latency, simplest datapath for VPC-to-VPC traffic. Downsides: broad routing visibility between VPCs (unless you use strict security group rules), cross-account peering limitations in some clouds, and harder to enforce per-service access controls. Good when both parties trust routing boundaries and want minimal added hops.

- PrivateLink (VPCE): strong isolation (endpoint per service), easy to scope access to a single service, easier to audit via endpoint usage logs. Potential latency overhead from NLB/endpoint proxies and sometimes limited to regional endpoints; also requires more operational setup (endpoint services + certificates). Favor if security/isolation + per-service access is top priority.

- Site-to-Site VPN: great for on-prem customers or when direct peering isn't allowed. Higher and more variable latency, less ideal for strict P95 SLAs. Good fallback when network topology or corporate policies block cloud-native constructs.

Observability & compliance notes:
- Peering: you must rely on VPC flow logs + packet logs from both sides; tie flows to service identity using source/destination tags. Access auditing is coarse unless you add per-service proxies.
- PrivateLink: gives cleaner per-endpoint logs and easier mapping to service-level audits (VPCE logs + Load Balancer logs). Certificate and mutual TLS posture important.
- VPN: central point for packet capture at the gateway, but middleboxes obscure per-service attribution. Encryption in transit is fine, but key rotation and IKE policies must be documented for audits.

Checklist I suggest your network team run (short):
1) Confirm whether cross-account peering is allowed between your VPC and our account (if peering).
2) Verify you can expose a VPCE endpoint service or prefer us to publish an endpoint in our account and share.
3) Measure baseline latency from your subnets to the candidate endpoint zone.
4) Confirm logging/flow retention and whether logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
5) Ask security about endpoint certificate requirements and mTLS expectations.

If helpful we can also stand up a short latency test pod in our staging region to provide numbers. Proposed next step: quick call Wed 10/14 10am PT to walk the matrix and align on security needs.

Do you want us to include an SLA draft to discuss in the same call?

Thanks,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational considerations from the Private product side:

- PrivateLink endpoint limits: some regions or accounts restrict number of VPCEs per service; if FinAssure has many VPCs, endpoint management can become a scaling task. Consider a shared transit VPC pattern for larger fleets.

- Certificate & MTLS: for PrivateLink we recommend mutual TLS at the application layer. For peering, mTLS should still be enforced on the service; peering alone doesn't provide per-service auth.

- Auto-scaling and connection churn: peering preserves direct TCP connections which can be more efficient for high-throughput bursty traffic. VPCE endpoints may front requests through NLBs which have connection limits and circuit-breaker behaviors to plan for.

- Fallbacks: we often recommend a primary (peering or PrivateLink) with a VPN fallback for emergency/maintenance windows. The fallback should be pre-configured but inactive to avoid routing flaps during failover.

Kimberly Park

Hi Alice — from a compliance and audit perspective here are a few additional items to validate:

- Log retention & immutability: confirm the retention window for VPC flow logs / VPCE logs and whether they can be exported to an immutable store (your SIEM or an audit bucket). We recommend 12 months minimum for regulated customers.
- Data residency: ensure any traffic that crosses regions is acceptable; PrivateLink is region-bound and can help enforce residency.
- Access reviews: we need to include a quarterly access review process if peering is used (to ensure no stale security-group rules).
- Pen test scope: if you're choosing peering, include the Redwoods endpoint in scope and confirm whether you want us to run a joint network-level pen test.

I attached an observability checklist and a short SLA draft for your legal team to skim.

— Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Private deployment networking — quick ask on best ingress pattern

Alice — thanks for the quick sync earlier today. Action items & recommendation summary below (we agreed this on the call):

Decision: start with PrivateLink in a single-region pilot for strong isolation and auditability; enable a peering path between a controlled staging VPC for low-latency testing, and keep a pre-configured VPN as a firebreak.

Why: PrivateLink gives per-endpoint observability and easier audit mapping (good for PII). Peering in staging lets you validate P95 without impacting production routing. VPN is the guaranteed fallback for maintenance or cross-region paths.

Action items (owners):
- FinAssure network: confirm VPCE quota and whether they prefer us to publish endpoint service or host in their account (Alice / Rajesh) — due 2026-10-20.
- FinAssure security: provide certificate / mTLS requirements and log retention policy — due 2026-10-20.
- Redwood (Nikhil): provide a latency test pod + sample throughput tests for your subnets (I’ll share credentials once we agree on IP allowlist) — due 2026-10-18.
- Redwood (Kimberly): share our recommended NLB tuning and connection limits for the PrivateLink fronting layer — due 2026-10-19.
- Redwood (Monica): share the observability checklist & SLA draft (attached) — done.

Attachments included: ingress-option-matrix.xlsx, network-observability-checklist.pdf, proposed-sla-draft.docx

If anything above looks off, reply-all and we’ll adjust. I’ll follow up with the latency pod details later today.

Best,
